lesson: Card #8 went 1W-0L for +$14.34 on the single pick — Manchester City's perfect record held up, winning 1-0 at Old Trafford. The three skips were also validated: Lens drew (not the win the model implied), and the pullback after Saturday's 0-5 was the right call. Today the pattern repeats in an interesting way: Villarreal are priced as favourites at home to Real Betis, but Betis just beat Real Madrid away and Villarreal are winless in three. Same lesson as Le Mans-Lens, opposite conclusion — this time the form points to backing the 'underdog'.

matches.analysis: FEATURED MATCH. Roma are 3 wins from 3 with 10 goals scored and only 1 conceded — the best record in Serie A, and unlike some short prices we've avoided, this one is backed by genuinely exceptional current numbers, not just reputation. Torino have lost 3 of 4 matches this season and are averaging under 8 shots a game. The price is short, but the gap in form is real and large.

Villarreal are the home 'favourite' on the model, but they're winless in three including a home defeat to Deportivo. Real Betis, meanwhile, just beat Real Madrid 1-0 away from home — a genuine statement result, not a fluke. This is today's version of yesterday's Lens lesson, just pointing the other way: the team with worse current form is priced as favourite, and the value sits with the side that's actually playing well.

Braga have kept a clean sheet in all four of their home matches this season; Estoril have failed to score in three of their last four games and remain winless across thirteen top-flight outings. Braga's straight win price (1.44) is too short to be worth backing outright, but the specific pattern here — a flawless home defence against a team that simply cannot score — is a cleaner, better-priced angle than the plain favourite bet.
Both sides are unbeaten in three, but both are also draw-heavy — Leeds have scored just once in each of their last three, Newcastle have drawn two of their last three. No clean edge either way. Pass.
